The particle "min" was inserted in His saying ﴿and between us and you is a barrier﴾, and the meaning is: "and between us and you is a barrier," for emphasis of the statement.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 6–7:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Say: I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your God is one God. So take a straight course to Him and seek His forgiveness. And woe to those who associate others with Allah (al-mushrikin), who do not give zakah and who, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to these who turn away from the signs of Allah among your people: O people, I am only a human being from the children of Adam like you in kind, form and appearance. I am not an angel. ﴿It is revealed to me﴾: Allah reveals to me that there is no deity deserving worship except one deity. ﴿So take a straight course to Him﴾: he says, take a straight course to Him in obedience, and turn your faces to Him in desire and worship, not to the gods and idols.

He says: And ask Him for pardon for your sins that have passed from you, through repentance from your polytheism; He will accept repentance from you and forgive you.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And woe to the associators, who do not give zakah and who, concerning the Hereafter, are disbelievers﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And the pus of the people of the Fire, and what flows from them, is for those who claim that Allah has partners, who worship idols besides Him, who do not give zakah.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding this. Some of them said: its meaning is: those who do not give Allah the obedience that purifies them and purifies their bodies, and who do not affirm His oneness. This is a statement reported from Ibn 'Abbas.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

- Ali narrated to me, he said: Abu Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿And woe to the associators, who do not give zakah﴾ he said: They are those who do not testify that there is no god but Allah.

- Sa'id ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, he said: Hafs narrated to us, he said: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿And woe to the associators, who do not give zakah﴾: those who do not say: there is no god but Allah.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: those who do not acknowledge the zakah on their wealth which Allah has enjoined on them, and do not give it to its recipients. We have also already mentioned those who said this.

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And woe to the associators, who do not give zakah﴾: he said: They do not acknowledge it and do not believe in it. It used to be said: zakah is the bridge of Islam; whoever cuts it off is saved, and whoever holds back from it is destroyed. The apostates after the Prophet of Allah said: As for prayer, we will pray; as for zakah, by Allah, our wealth will not be taken. He said: Abu Bakr said: By Allah, I will not separate between things that Allah has joined together; by Allah, if they withheld from me even a rope (iqal) of what Allah and His Messenger enjoined, we would fight them over it.

- Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And woe to the associators, who do not give zakah﴾: he said: Even if they gave zakah while they were associators, it would not benefit them.

The correct view on this matter is what those said who stated that its meaning is: they do not pay the zakah of their wealth. This is because that is the more well-known meaning of zakah, and because His saying ﴿and, concerning the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾ is evidence that this is so. The disbelievers intended by this verse did not testify that there is no god but Allah. So if His saying ﴿who do not give zakah﴾ were meant as those who do not testify that there is no god but Allah, His saying ﴿and, concerning the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾ would have no meaning, since it is known that whoever does not testify that there is no god but Allah does not believe in the Hereafter. Allah's following His saying ﴿and, concerning the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾ with His saying ﴿who do not give zakah﴾ indicates that zakah in this place refers to the zakah of wealth.

The commentary on the words of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward that will never end (8). Say, "Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds" (9).﴾

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed, those who affirm God and His Messenger, and act upon what God and His Messenger have commanded them, and refrain from what He has forbidden them, and that is what is meant by "righteous deeds." ﴿They will have a reward that will never end﴾ means: for those who do that, there is a reward that is not diminished from what He promised to recompense them with.

The exegetes have differed regarding the interpretation of this, and we have explained it previously in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary in this place. And:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They will have a reward that will never end﴾: Some of them said: "not diminished." And some of them said: "not reckoned as a favour upon them."

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿a reward that will never end﴾, he said: "not diminished."

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, regarding His words: ﴿They will have a reward that will never end﴾, he said: "counted."

That refers to Sunday and Monday. Reports from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) have come concerning this, and the scholars have stated it. We have mentioned much of that previously, and we shall mention some of what we did not mention before, God willing.

Mention of some of the reports on this which we did not mention previously:

* Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said, Hannad said: I read the rest of the hadith to Abu Bakr: "The Jews came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: 'God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and He created the mountains on Tuesday and what is in them of benefits, and on Wednesday He created the trees, the water, the cities, and the civilisation and ruin; these are four.' Then he said: ﴿Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days, and attribute to Him equals? It has been mentioned from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to read this: "wa qassama fiha aqwatha-ha" (and He apportioned therein its sustenances).

The people of Arabic have differed on the grammatical basis of the fatha in sawa'an. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: whoever reads it with a fatha makes it a verbal noun (masdar), as if he said: istiwa'. He said: it has also been read with a kasra and made a noun for the equal things: i.e. in four complete days. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: whoever reads it with a kasra makes it an attribute of the days, and if you wish, of the four; and whoever reads it with a fatha makes it connected to the sustenances. He said: it may also be read with a damma, as if it were a beginning (mubtada'), as if he said: that is ﴿alike for those who ask﴾, meaning: for whoever wishes to know it.

The correct view on this is that when it is read with a fatha it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) of the sustenances, since sawa' has been likened to indefinite nouns, so it is said: "I passed by a people sawa'" (equal), and it follows indefinite nouns; and when it follows indefinite nouns it is detached from the definites and put in the accusative, so it is said: "I passed by your brothers sawa'." It may also be that when no dual or plural is applied to it, it is likened to verbal nouns. As for when it is read with a damma, it is only a beginning with the pronoun of "that" and the like; and when it is read with a kasra, it follows the days or the four.

He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿in four days﴾, according to what we mentioned earlier of the report we related from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), that he finished creating the earth and all its causes and benefits, of trees, water, cities, settlement and ruin, in four days, the first of which is Sunday and the last of which is Wednesday.

⁕ Musa narrated to me, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: He created the mountains in it, and the sustenance of its people, its trees, and what befits it, in two days, on Tuesday and Wednesday.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said: He created the earth in two days, then He said: in four days, because He means that this, together with the first, makes four days, as you say: "I married a woman yesterday, and today two," and one of them is the one you married yesterday.

* *

His words: ﴿alike for those who ask﴾

The interpreters differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: its interpretation is: alike for whoever asks about the term in which God created the earth, placed in it the firm mountains above it and the blessing, and measured therein the sustenance for its people; he will find it as God informed: four days, neither more nor less than that.

Those who said this:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿alike for those who ask﴾ — whoever asks about it will find it as God said.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: ﴿alike for those who ask﴾ — he said: whoever asks will find it as God said.

⁕ Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿in four days, alike for those who ask﴾ — he says: whoever asks, the matter is thus.

Others said: rather its meaning is: alike for whoever asks his Lord for anything he needs of provision, for God has measured for him of sustenance in the earth, according to the request of each asker of them, had he asked, since nothing of His knowledge about them had passed before He created them.

Those who said this:

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words ﴿alike for those who ask﴾ — he said: He measured that according to their requests, knowing that nothing of their requests occurs except what He had known before it occurred. The reciters differed concerning the recitation of this. The common reciters of the metropolises, except Abu Ja'far and al-Hasan al-Basri, read ﴿sawa'an﴾ with a fatha. Abu Ja'far the reciter read "sawa'un" with a damma. al-Hasan read "sawa'in" with a kasra.

The correct recitation in this is what the reciters of the metropolises hold, namely its reading with a fatha, for the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it, and for the soundness of its meaning. That is because the meaning of the speech is: He measured therein its sustenance, alike for its askers, according to what they need and what sets them right.

It has been mentioned from Ibn Mas'ud that he used to read this: "wa qassama fiha aqwatha-ha" (and He apportioned therein its sustenances).

The people of Arabic have differed on the grammatical basis of the fatha in sawa'an. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: whoever reads it with a fatha makes it a verbal noun (masdar), as if he said: istiwa'. He said: it has also been read with a kasra and made a noun for the equal things: i.e. in four complete days. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: whoever reads it with a kasra makes it an attribute of the days, and if you wish, of the four; and whoever reads it with a fatha makes it connected to the sustenances. He said: it may also be read with a damma, as if it were a beginning (mubtada'), as if he said: that is ﴿alike for those who ask﴾, meaning: for whoever wishes to know it.

The correct view on this is that when it is read with a fatha it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) of the sustenances, since sawa' has been likened to indefinite nouns, so it is said: "I passed by a people sawa'" (equal), and it follows indefinite nouns; and when it follows indefinite nouns it is detached from the definites and put in the accusative, so it is said: "I passed by your brothers sawa'." It may also be that when no dual or plural is applied to it, it is likened to verbal nouns. As for when it is read with a damma, it is only a beginning with the pronoun of "that" and the like; and when it is read with a kasra, it follows the days or the four.

* *

His words: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly."﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: then He turned to the heaven, then rose up to the heaven.

We have already set out the statements of the people of knowledge on this earlier.

His words: ﴿and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly"﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: God said to the heaven and the earth: "Bring forth what I created in you both. As for you, O heaven, make appear what I created in you of the sun, the moon and the stars; and as for you, O earth, bring out what I created in you of trees, fruits and plants, and split open for rivers." ﴿They said: "We come willingly"﴾: "We bring what You have produced in us of Your creation, submitting to Your command, not disobeying Your order."

Interpreters have said the like of what we have said on this.

Those who said this:

⁕ Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Sulayman ibn Musa, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿and said to it and to the earth: "Come both of you, willingly or unwillingly." They said: "We come willingly"﴾ — he said: God said to the heavens: "Make rise my sun and my moon, and make rise my stars"; and He said to the earth: "Split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits." They said: "We give willingly."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Sulayman al-Ahwal, from Tawus, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His word ﴿i'tiya﴾ (come): "give"; and concerning His word ﴿qalata atayna﴾ (they said: "we came"): they said: "we gave."

It was said: "atayna ta'i'in" (we came willingly), and He did not say "ta'i'atayn", though the heaven and the earth are feminine, because the nun and the alif which are the pronoun of their names in His word ﴿atayna﴾ are like the pronoun of men's names when they speak of themselves; so He made His word ﴿ta'i'in﴾ run as the report about men runs. Some of the grammarians of Arabic used to say: it is directed to the heavens and the earth and those within them.

Others among them said: it is said so because when the two spoke, they resembled the males of the sons of Adam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 12:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens within two days, and inspired in each heaven its command. And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ (12).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: He finished creating them as seven heavens in two days, and these are Thursday and Friday.

As follows:

* Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, from the breath of the water when it breathed. So He made it one heaven, then He split it and made it seven heavens in two days, on Thursday and Friday. The day was called Friday (al-Jumu'ah) only because on it the creation of the heavens and the earth was gathered (jama'a)."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and inspired in each heaven its command﴾

He says: He cast into each of the seven heavens what He willed of creation.

Those of the exegetical tradition (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and inspired in each heaven its command﴾, he said: "What Allah commanded and willed."

* Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and inspired in each heaven its command﴾, he said: "He created in each heaven that He created from the angels and the creation that is in it, from the seas and the mountains of hail, and what is not known."

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and inspired in each heaven its command﴾: "He created in it its sun, its moon, its stars, and their good order."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿And We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps and as protection﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We adorned the nearest heaven for you, O people, with the stars, which are the lamps.

As follows:

* Musa related to us, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿We adorned the nearest heaven with lamps﴾, he said: "Then He adorned the heaven with the stars, making them an adornment ﴿and as protection﴾ from the devils."

The grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyyah) differed on the case of His saying ﴿wa-hifzan﴾ (and as protection). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: it is in the accusative with the meaning: "And We guarded it as a guarding," as if He said: "And We guard it with a guarding," because when He said "We adorned it with lamps," He had informed that He had looked into its affair and watched over it, and this indicates protection, as if He said: "And We guarded it as a guarding." Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: it is in the accusative on the meaning: "and [We adorned it] as protection," meaning "We adorned it," because if the conjunction were dropped, it would be "Indeed We adorned the nearest heaven as protection." This second view is closer to correctness in our opinion than the first.

We have explained the reason for the like of this in more than one place in this book, so that suffices and there is no need to repeat it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: This which I have described to you of My creation of the heaven and the earth and what is in them, and My adornment of the nearest heaven with the adornment of the stars, is the decree of the Almighty in His vengeance upon His enemies, the All-Knowing of the secrets and the open affairs of His servants, and of their arrangements in what is good for them.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 41, verses 13–14:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away, then say: "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd."﴾ ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them, saying: "Worship none but Allah." They said: "If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels. So indeed we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: If these polytheists turn away from this proof which I have made clear to them, O Muhammad, and which you have pointed out to them, and they do not believe in it nor acknowledge that the Doer of that is Allah, there is no god besides Him, then say to them: "I warn you, O people, of a thunderbolt that will destroy you, like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd."

We have already explained earlier that the meaning of ṣāʿiqah (thunderbolt, a term meaning anything that corrupts a thing and changes it from its condition) is everything that corrupts a thing and alters it from its form. It has been said that in this place it refers to a destruction from Allah and a punishment.

Those who said this:

Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah, regarding His words ﴿a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd﴾, he said: It means: "I have warned you of a destruction like the destruction of ʿĀd and Thamūd." He said: a punishment like the punishment of ʿĀd and Thamūd.

* *

And His words: ﴿When the messengers came to them from before them and from behind them﴾

It means: say, "I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ʿĀd and Thamūd that destroyed them, when the messengers came to ʿĀd and Thamūd from before them and from behind them." So His words "when" (idh) are connected to "thunderbolt."

By His words ﴿from before them﴾ is meant the messengers who came to the fathers of those who were destroyed by the thunderbolt from these two nations.

By His words ﴿and from behind them﴾ is meant: from behind the messengers who were sent to their fathers, sending messengers to them. This is because Allah sent Hūd to ʿĀd, and they denied him after messengers had already been sent before him to their fathers as well, and they denied them too, so they were destroyed.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-taʾwīl) have said something similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words ﴿But if they turn away﴾ ... to His words ﴿and from behind them﴾, he said: "The messengers who were before Hūd, and the messengers who came after him. Allah sent messengers before him and sent messengers after him."

* *

And His words: ﴿Worship none but Allah﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: the messengers came to them saying that they should worship none but Allah, alone, without partner.

They said: ﴿If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels﴾. He, whose praise is great, says: They said to their messengers when they called them to acknowledge the oneness of Allah: "If our Lord had willed that we affirm His oneness and not worship anything other than Him, He would have sent down to us angels from heaven as messengers with what you call us to. He did not send you, though you are humans like us, but He was pleased with our worship of what we worship, and therefore He did not send angels to us to forbid that."

* *

And His words: ﴿So indeed we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent﴾

He says: They said to their messengers: "Indeed we reject what your Lord has sent you with to us, disbelieving in it and not confirming it."

**The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 41, Verse 16**

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind in days of ill omen, that We might let them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world. But the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing, and they will not be helped﴾.

He, exalted is His mention, says: "So We sent upon 'Ad a furious wind."

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of *al-sarsar* (furious). Some of them said: it means a wind that is intense.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿a furious wind﴾, he said: "Intense."
- al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿a furious wind﴾: "Intense in its scorching heat upon them."

Others said: rather, it means that it was cold.

Those who said this:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿So We sent upon them a furious wind﴾, he said: "*Al-sarsar*: the cold one."
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿a furious wind﴾, he said: "Cold."
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿a furious wind﴾, he said: "Cold, having a sound."
- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿a furious wind﴾, he says: "A wind in which there is intense cold."

The most correct of the two opinions is the opinion of Mujahid, because His words ﴿*sarsaran*﴾ are only the sound of the wind when it blows with force, so a sound is heard from it like the saying of the speaker: *sarr*. Then this was made into a form with doubling in the *ra'*, and one of the *ra'*s was changed into a *sad* because of the many *ra'*s, as it is said in *radrada* (to repel) becoming *radrada*, and in *nahnaha* (to restrain), as Ru'ba said:

*Today he restrains me,*
*and the first of forbearance is not with the foolish one*

[[The two verses are in his Diwan (Leipzig edition, p. 166), and they are verses 19 and 20. *Nahnanī* means he rebuked me and restrained me. He says this after he has grown old and weak. *Al-awwal* means return. *Al-hilm* means intellect. *Al-sufah*: that which is attributed to foolishness. He says: I used to respond to the calls of youth as long as I was young; but today, now that old age has overtaken me, and he has returned to what has departed from his intellect, my forbearance and my intellect have restrained me from frivolity, so I do not do what I used to do in youth.]]

And as it is said in *kaffahu*: *kafkafahu* (to restrain), as al-Nabigha said:

*I restrain a tear that has overcome my enemies;*
*when I restrain it, it returns as a slaughter*

[[The author attributed this verse to al-Nabigha, but I did not find it in the Diwan or in its various commentaries. The meaning of *ukafkifu al-'abrah* is: I turn it back. His words *ghalabat 'udatī* mean: they were eager that I should weep so that they might harm me with that; so my tear, which I had held back, overcame them. *Nahnahtuhā* means: I restrained it and turned it back. *Dhibāḥan* means slaughter. He means that he held back his tear, and holding it back was like slaughter because of the intensity of the pain, since weeping eases what burns within the soul of pain, anger and the like. The verse, in the author's view, is evidence that *kafkafa*, *nahnaha* and *sarsara* and the like come from the quadriliteral doubled verb; their original forms are: *kafaf*, *nahah* and *sarar*. When three identical letters came together in it, one of the *ra'*s was changed into a letter of the same kind as the first radical of the word. This is the view of some of the Kufan grammarians, and God knows best.]]

It has been said: the river called *Sarsar* was only named so because of the sound of the water flowing in it, and that it is *fa'lal* from *sarra*, like the furious wind (*al-rīh al-sarsar*).

* *

And His words: ﴿in days of ill omen﴾

The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of *al-nahsat*. Some of them said: it means consecutive ones.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿in days of ill omen﴾, he said: "Consecutive days in which God sent down the punishment."

Others said: it means the ill-omened ones.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Waraqa narrated to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿days of ill omen﴾, he said: "Ill-omened."
- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, ﴿in days of ill omen﴾: "Days which, by God, were ill-omened upon the people."
- Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatada, who said: "*Al-nahsat*: the ill-omened, the wretched ones."
- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿in days of ill omen﴾, he said: "Days ill-omened for them."

Others said: the meaning of that is: days containing evil.

Those who said this:

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿days of ill omen﴾: "*Al-nahs* is evil. He sent upon them a wind of evil in which there was nothing of good."

Others said: *al-nahsat* are the severe ones.

Those who said this:

- I was told by al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say ﴿in days of ill omen﴾, he said: "Severe."

The most correct of the opinions regarding this is the opinion of the one who said that it means: days of ill omen, possessing misfortunes, because that is the known meaning of *al-nahs* in the speech of the Arabs.

The readers (qira') have differed in the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of the great cities, other than Nafi' and Abu Amr, recite ﴿fī ayyāmin naḥisāt﴾ with a kasra on the *ha'*. Nafi' and Abu Amr recite *naḥsāt* with a sukun (silence) on the *ha'*. Abu Amr, as has been reported to us from him, used to argue for his sukun on the *ha'* by the words of Him: ﴿a day of continuous ill omen (yawmi naḥsin mustamirr)﴾, where the *ha'* is silent.

The correct statement on this is that it is said: they are two well-known readings, and each of them has been recited by learned readers, while their meanings agree. That is because the vocalisation of the *ha'* with a dammah and its silencing are two known dialects. It is said: *hādhā yawmun naḥsun* and *yawmun naḥisun*, with a kasra on the *ha'* and with its silence. Al-Farra' said: some of the Arabs recited to me:

*Convey to Judham and Lakhm*
*that their brothers, Tayy and Bahra',*
*a people whose help is ill-omened*

[[This verse is one of al-Farra's evidences in his Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 289), at His words: "in days of ill omen". He said: the common people pronounce it with a heavy *ha'* with a kasra. Some of the people of Medina lightened it (with a sukun on the *ha'*). He said: I have heard some of the Arabs recite: "Convey to Judham..." This is for the one who makes it heavy. *Two days of cloud, and a day of sun,*
*two stars with good fortune, and a star of ill omen*

So whoever in his dialect says *yawmun naḥsun* says *fī ayyāmin naḥsāt*, and whoever in his dialect says ﴿yawmi naḥsin﴾ says ﴿fī ayyāmin naḥisāt﴾. He, exalted is His praise, says: And Our punishment of them in the Hereafter is more disgracing for them and more severe in humiliation and abasement. He says: and they, meaning 'Ad, will not be helped by anyone from God on the Day of Resurrection, when He punishes them, so that no helper can rescue them from Him, or take vengeance for them.

As related:

* Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾: that is, We made clear to them.

* Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾: We made clear to them the path of good and evil.

* Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾: We made clear to them.

* Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾: He said: We informed them of guidance and error, we forbade them from following error, and we commanded them to follow guidance.

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words: ﴿Thamud﴾. The majority of reciters in the regions read it with a nominative ending (raf') and without diptotic inflection (tark al-ijra'), treating it as the name of the nation known by that name. As for al-A'mash and Abdullah ibn Abi Ishaq, [it is reported that] al-A'mash used to inflect it throughout the Qur'an except in His words: ﴿And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign﴾, where he did not inflect it specifically in this place, because in the Mushaf's script it is written here without an alif; and he would construe Thamud as the name of a specific, well-known man, or the name of a well-known tribe. As for Ibn Ishaq, he read it in the accusative (nasb). As for Thamud without inflection, although it has a known basis in Arabic, the more eloquent and more correct in grammar according to the grammarians is the nominative, because of the requirement that ammā be followed by nouns and that verbs do not follow it; the Arabs only make the verbs after the nouns operative when it is good to place them before the noun, and the verb after ammā cannot properly be placed before the noun. Do you not see that one does not say: "wa-ammā hadaynā fa-Thamud," as one says: ﴿As for Thamud, We guided them﴾?

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the nominative with no inflection: the nominative for what has been described, and the absence of inflection because it is the name of a nation.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾, he said: "You did not fear."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And you did not suppose."

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾, he says: "And you did not suppose ﴿lest your hearing testify against you or your sight﴾" up to ﴿much of what﴾ you [[The apparent reading is that the word "kuntum" was added in error by the author in both places.]] ﴿do﴾. Whoever can die while having a good opinion of Allah should do so, and there is no power except through Allah.

The most correct of these sayings, in the view of the truth, is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: "And you did not hide [from guilt]," so that you would abandon committing the prohibitions of Allah in the world, out of fear that your hearing and your sight would testify against you today.

We have said that this is the most correct of these sayings because the well-known meaning of *istitar* is *istikhfa'* (concealment, hiding oneself).

If someone says: How does a person hide from himself what he is about to do? It is said: We have already explained that its meaning is the wishes, and in abandoning doing it there is a concealing of it from himself.

As for His words: (But you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you [[The apparent reading is that the word "kuntum" was added in error by the author in both places.]] do), He, may His praise be exalted, says: But you thought, when you committed the disobediences of Allah in the world, that Allah does not know much of your evil deeds, and therefore you did not conceal yourselves from your hearing, your sight and your skins testifying against you, so that you would abandon committing what Allah has forbidden you.

(21) And you did not conceal yourselves [from guilt] lest your hearing testify against you or your sight or your skins, but you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you do.﴾ (22)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And those enemies of Allah, the glorified, who are gathered to the Fire will say to their skins, when they testify against them about what they used to do in the world: "Why did you testify against us about what we used to do in the world?"

Their skins will answer them: ﴿Allah has caused us to speak, He who causes everything to speak﴾, so we spoke. It is mentioned that these limbs testify against their owners when Allah makes them witnesses against them, when they deny the deeds they had done in the world that displeased Allah. And this has come in the report from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Mention of the reports transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ:

* Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Qadim al-Fazari informed us, he said: Sharik informed us, from ʿUbayd al-Mukatib, from al-Shaʿbi, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ laughed one day until his molar teeth showed, then he said: "Will you not ask me what I laughed at?" They said: "What did you laugh at, Messenger of Allah?" He said: "I marvelled at the servant's disputing with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection! He says: 'O Lord, did You not promise me that You would not wrong me?' He says: 'Indeed, that is so.' He says: 'Then I do not accept any witness against myself except from myself.' He says: 'Is it not sufficient that I am a witness against you, and the honourable recording angels?' He says: Then a seal will be placed upon his mouth, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do. He says: Then he says to them: 'Away with you, be destroyed! It was for you that I was disputing.'"

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Mihran narrated to us, from Sufyan, from ʿUbayd al-Mukatib, from Fudayl ibn ʿAmr, from al-Shaʿbi, from Anas, from the Prophet ﷺ, with a similar report.

* ʿAbbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, he said: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr narrated to us, from Shibl, who said: I heard Abu Qaz'a narrate to ʿAmr ibn Dinar, from Hakim ibn Muʿawiya, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said, and he pointed with his hand towards Syria: "From here to here you will be gathered, riding and on foot, upon your faces on the Day of Resurrection, with a gag upon your mouths. You will be the seventy nations, you being the last of them and the most honoured of them before Allah. And the first thing of you to speak will be his thigh."

* Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: al-Hariri informed us, from Hakim ibn Muʿawiya, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "And you will come on the Day of Resurrection with a gag upon your mouths, and the first thing of the human being to speak will be his thigh and his palm."

* Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Bahz ibn Hakim, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "What is the matter with me that I hold you back by your waistbands from the Fire? Indeed my Lord is calling, and He will ask me whether I conveyed to His servants; and I will say: 'My Lord, I have conveyed to them.' So let the present one convey to the absent one. Then you will be called, your mouths sealed with a gag, and the first part of you that will speak will be his thigh and his palm."

* Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me, he said: al-Haytham ibn Kharija narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, from Dhamdham ibn Zur'a, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from 'Uqba, who heard the Prophet ﷺ say: "The first bone of the human being to speak on the Day when the mouths are sealed is his thigh, from the left leg."

* *

And His words: ﴿And it is He who created you the first time﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah created you with the first creation when you were nothing. He means: and to Him is your return after your death. ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾ in the world ﴿lest your hearing testify against you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection ﴿or your sight or your skins﴾.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: "And you did not hide yourselves."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾: i.e., you did not hide yourselves from them.

Others said: its meaning is: "And you did not fear."

Those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾, he said: "You did not fear."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is: "And you did not suppose."

Those who said that:

* Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾, he says: "And you did not suppose ﴿lest your hearing testify against you or your sight﴾" up to ﴿much of what﴾ you [[The apparent reading is that the word "kuntum" was added in error by the author in both places.]] ﴿do﴾. By Allah, indeed upon you, O son of Adam, are witnesses from your own body who are not accused, so be watchful over them and fear Allah in your secret and open affairs, for nothing is hidden from Him; darkness is light before Him, and secret is open before Him. Whoever can die while having a good opinion of Allah should do so, and there is no power except through Allah.

The most correct of these sayings, in the view of the truth, is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of that is: "And you did not hide [from guilt]," so that you would abandon committing the prohibitions of Allah in the world, out of fear that your hearing and your sight would testify against you today.

We have said that this is the most correct of these sayings because the well-known meaning of *istitar* is *istikhfa'* (concealment, hiding oneself).

If someone says: How does a person hide from himself what he is about to do? It is said: We have already explained that its meaning is the wishes, and in abandoning doing it there is a concealing of it from himself.

As for His words: (But you assumed that Allah does not know much of what you [[The apparent reading is that the word "kuntum" was added in error by the author in both places.]] do), He, may His praise be exalted, says: But you thought, when you committed the disobediences of Allah in the world, that Allah does not know much of your evil deeds, and therefore you did not conceal yourselves from your hearing, your sight and your skins testifying against you, so that you would abandon committing what Allah has forbidden you.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of men who disputed among themselves about Allah's knowledge of what they said and spoke in secret.

The report concerning that:

* Ibn Yahya al-Qati'i narrated to me, he said: Abu Dawud narrated to us, he said: Qays narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar al-Azdi, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I was hiding behind the curtains of the Ka'ba, when three men entered, two Thaqafis and a Qurashi, or two Qurashis and a Thaqafi, with much fat on their bellies and little understanding in their hearts. They spoke words I did not understand. One of them said: "Do you think that Allah hears what we say?" The two said: "If we raise our voices, He hears; if we do not raise them, He does not hear." So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him of that, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing testify against you or your sight﴾ ... to the end of the verse.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, he said: al-A'mash narrated to me, from 'Umara ibn 'Umayr, from Wahb ibn Rabi'a, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I was hiding behind the curtains of the Ka'ba when three men entered, a Thaqafi and his two in-laws, both Qurashis, little understanding in their hearts, much fat on their bellies. They talked among themselves, and one of them said: "Do you think Allah hears what we say?" The other said: "He hears if we raise our voices, and does not hear if we lower them." Another said: "If He hears some of it, He hears all of it." So I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and told him of that, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing testify against you or your sight﴾ ... up to ﴿And if they ask to be shown favour, they will not be among those shown favour﴾.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: Yahya narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, he said: Mansur narrated to me, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from Abdullah, with a similar report.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 23:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you, and you have become among the losers.﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: This which was from you in the world, of your assumption that Allah does not know much of what you do of your vile deeds and wrongdoings, is the assumption you assumed about your Lord in the world, which has destroyed you, meaning, has caused your ruin. It is said of it: "Ardā fulānan kadhā wa kadhā" (he destroyed so-and-so such-and-such) if he caused him to perish, and "radiya huwa" (he perished) if he died, so he is "yuradā radan" (perishes in ruin). And from it is the saying of al-A'sha:

"Did you fear for me the ruin (al-radā) in the journey? And how many a ruin has destroyed its people without it being considered?"

[This verse is by al-A'sha, addressing his daughter. The matter has already been discussed at length in Part 23 (p. 62). The point of evidence here is "al-radā" in the sense of destruction. It is a verbal noun of radiya (like fariḥa), yuradā radan. And from it is His saying, exalted is He: "And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you."]

Meaning: And how many a perisher has destroyed his people, he was not turned away.

And with what we have said concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have spoken.

Mention of those who said that:

- Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿it has destroyed you﴾, he said: it has caused your ruin.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, he said: al-Hasan recited: ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you﴾ and said: People act only according to the measure of their assumptions about their Lord. As for the believer, he thought well of Allah, so he did well in deeds; and as for the disbeliever and the hypocrite, they thought ill, so they did ill in deeds. Your Lord said: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing and your sight and your skins testify against you﴾ ... until: "the losers." Ma'mar said: A man also narrated to me that a man will be ordered to the Fire, and he will turn and say: "O Lord, this was not my assumption of You." He will say: "And what was your assumption of Me?" He will say: "My assumption was that You would forgive me and not punish me." He will say: "I am according to your assumption of Me."

- Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: Assumption is of two kinds: an assumption that saves, and an assumption that destroys. He said: ﴿Those who assume that they will meet their Lord﴾ and ﴿Indeed, I assumed that I would meet my account﴾. This saving assumption is certain assumption. And he said here: ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you﴾. This is the assumption that destroys.

And His words: ﴿And those who disbelieve said: We assume only an assumption, and we are not among the certain.﴾ It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say, relating it from his Lord: "My servant is according to his assumption of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me."

The place of His words ﴿That﴾ is in the nominative case, governed by "your assumption" (zannukum). When that is so, His words ﴿it has destroyed you﴾ occupy the accusative place, meaning: destroying you. It may also be possible that it is in the nominative place by way of a new sentence, meaning: destroying you, as He said: ﴿Those are the verses of the Wise Book, a guidance and mercy﴾ in the reading of one who reads it in the nominative. So the meaning of the statement is: this assumption which you assumed about your Lord, that He does not know much of what you do, is what has destroyed you, for because of this assumption you dared against the prohibitions of Allah and advanced upon them, and committed what Allah forbade you, and that destroyed you and caused your ruin. He says: So you have become today among the perishers, having been cheated by selling your dwellings in Paradise for the dwellings of the people of Hellfire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 24:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whether they endure, the Fire is their dwelling place; and if they ask to be granted favor, they will not be among those granted favor.﴾ (41:24)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: If these people who are gathered to the Fire endure the Fire, then the Fire is their dwelling and abode. He says: And if they ask for al-'utba (the granting of favor), which is their return to what they love by lightening the punishment from them, then they are not of the people who are returned to Paradise so that the torment they are in is lightened for them. This is like His saying, majestic is His praise, reporting about them: ﴿They said: Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us...﴾ up to His saying ﴿and do not speak to me﴾, and like their saying to the guardians of Hell: ﴿Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment﴾ ... up to His saying: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 25:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And We appointed for them companions, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word became due against them, among nations that had passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾

He, may He be exalted, means by His words ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾: And We sent to them counterparts from the devils, and We made them their companions, pairing them with them, so that they would make their foul deeds seem attractive to them, and they made those things seem attractive to them.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾, he said: the devil.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾, he said: devils.

* *

As for His words ﴿and they made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them﴾:

He says: The companions among the devils made attractive to these disbelievers the matters of this world that lay before them. They beautified these for them and made them beloved to them, until they preferred them over the affair of the Hereafter. ﴿And what was behind them﴾ means: They also made attractive to them what would come after their death, by calling them to deny the Return, and [telling them] that whoever perished among them would never be resurrected, and that there is neither reward nor punishment, until they affirmed them in that; and they made easy for them the doing of everything they desired and the indulgence in every pleasure they enjoyed of immoralities, through their own approval of that for themselves.

And those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿and they made attractive to them what was before them﴾ of the affairs of this world, ﴿and what was behind them﴾ of the affairs of the Hereafter.

* *

As for His words ﴿and the word became due against them﴾:

He, may He be exalted, says: The punishment became due for them by their committing what they committed, which their companions among the devils had made attractive to them.

As [al-Suddi reported]:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿and the word became due against them﴾, he said: the punishment. ﴿among nations that had passed away before them of jinn and mankind﴾: He, may He be exalted, says: The punishment of Ours became due upon these whom We appointed companions from the devils, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, just as it became due upon those nations that had passed away before them, their like, some of them from the jinn and some of them from mankind.

﴿Indeed, they were losers﴾ means: Indeed those nations upon whom Our punishment became due, from the jinn and mankind, were defrauded, by selling the pleasure of Allah and His mercy for His wrath and punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 26–27:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome."﴾ [41:26] ﴿But We will surely cause those who disbelieve to taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do.﴾ [41:27]

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿And those who disbelieve﴾ in Allah and His Messenger, from the polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it"﴾. That is: they said to those who obey them among their allies from the polytheists, "Do not listen to the reciter of this Qur'an when he recites it, do not give ear to it, and do not follow what is in it so that you act upon it."

As related:

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome."﴾ He said: This is the statement of the polytheists; they said, "Do not follow this Qur'an, and turn away from it."

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿and talk noisily during it﴾

It means: utter vain speech when you hear its reciter reciting it, so that you do not hear it and do not understand what is in it.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾. He said: It is whistling and clapping, and confusing speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recites; Quraysh used to do this.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿and talk noisily during it﴾. He said: With whistling, clapping, and confusing speech against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he recites the Qur'an; Quraysh used to do this.

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it"﴾: meaning, deny it, reject it, and oppose it. He said: This is the statement of the polytheists of the Arabs.

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, who said: Some of them said regarding His saying: ﴿and talk noisily during it﴾: they talk loudly and shout so that you do not hear it.

* * *

As for His saying: ﴿that you may overcome﴾

It means: by doing that, you may turn away those who wish to listen to it from listening, so that they do not hear it; and if they do not hear it or understand it, they will not follow it, and thus you will overcome Muhammad through your action.

Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿But We will surely cause those who disbelieve﴾ in Allah from the polytheists of Quraysh who said this statement ﴿to taste a severe punishment﴾ in the Hereafter. ﴿And We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do﴾. That is: and We will reward them for that action and their other actions with the worst recompense for the deeds they performed in the world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 28:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity; a recompense for what they used to deny of Our signs.ﴩ (41:28)

His, the Exalted's, saying means: This recompense with which these disbelievers among the polytheists of Quraysh are repaid is the recompense of the enemies of Allah. Then He, may His praise be glorified, began a report about the description of that recompense and what it is, saying: "It is the Fire." So "the Fire" is an explanation of the recompense and a rendering of it, and it is in the nominative case by being a predicate to what precedes it. Then He said: ﴿For them therein is the abode of eternity﴾, meaning: for these polytheists who associate others with Allah, in the Fire is the abode of eternity, meaning the abode of staying and remaining, without end and without limit. The "abode" which He, may His praise be glorified, reported to be theirs in the Fire is the Fire itself, and this is acceptable because the two expressions differ, just as one says: "For you from your town there is a good abode, and from Kufa a noble abode," where the "abode" is Kufa and the town, and this is acceptable because the wording differs. It has also been reported to us that in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire, the abode of eternity," and in that is confirmation of what we have said in interpretation of this, namely that he rendered "the abode" as an explanation of "the Fire."

* *

And His saying: ﴿a recompense for what they used to deny of Our signs﴾

He says: We did this which We did to these people, by requiting them with the Fire for their deeds, as a recompense from Us for their denial in the world of Our signs by which We argued against them.

The commentary on His words, "And those who disbelieve will say, 'Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and mankind; we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest.'" (41:29)

He, exalted is His mention, says: And those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger will say on the Day of Resurrection, after they have been made to enter Hell: "O our Lord, show us those who misled us from Your creation, from among the jinn and mankind." It was said: the one from among the jinn is Iblis, and the one from among mankind is the son of Adam who killed his brother.

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Thabit al-Haddad, from Habba al-'Urani [[As in the Khulasah of al-Khazraji: Habba ibn Juwayn al-'Urani, with a damma on the first unpointed letter, Abu Qudamah al-Kufi; he narrated from Ali, and from him Salamah ibn Kuhayl and al-Hakam ibn Utaybah. Al-Ajli said: reliable. Ibn Sa'd said: he died in the year seventy-six. * *

As for His words, "we will put them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest":

He says: we will place these two who misled us beneath our feet, because the gates of Hell are some lower than others, and whatever is lower of them is more severe upon its people, and the punishment of its people is harsher. Therefore these disbelievers asked their Lord to show them those who misled them, so that they might place them below themselves, so that they would be in the most severe punishment, in the lowest rank of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 30:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast—the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised."﴾ (41:30)

His, may He be exalted and remembered, words: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ mean: [who testify that] He alone, with no partner, is Lord, and who renounce the gods and rivals [that are worshipped besides Him]. ﴿Then remain steadfast﴾ means: they remain steadfast upon the monotheism of Allah, do not mix the monotheism of Allah with associating others with Him, and adhere to His obedience in what He has commanded and forbidden.

The report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) agrees with what we have said, and the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have also said this, though they differ concerning the meaning of His words ﴿then remain steadfast﴾. The report on this from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is mentioned:

* Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, saying: Salim ibn Qutaybah Abu Qutaybah narrated to us, saying: Suhayl ibn Abi Hazm al-Qati'i narrated to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ and said: "People have said it, then most of them disbelieved. Whoever dies upon it is among those who remained steadfast."

Some of them said: its meaning is: they did not associate anything with Him, but they persevered upon monotheism.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Imran, who said: I recited this verse in the presence of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾, and he said: They are those who did not associate anything with Allah.

* Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan with his chain, from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, the like of it.

* Jarir ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, and Abd Allah ibn Idris, from al-Shaybani, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, that Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said to his companions: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: They said, "Our Lord is Allah," then acted upon it. He said: You have carried it to other than its proper meaning. ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾ are those who did not equate it with associating partners or anything else.

* Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Idris narrated to us, saying: al-Shaybani informed us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal al-Muharibi, who said: Abu Bakr said: What do you say about this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾? He said: "Our Lord is Allah," then they remained steadfast from sin. He said: Abu Bakr said: You have carried it to other than its proper meaning. They said: "Our Lord is Allah," then they remained steadfast and did not turn to any god other than Him.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Layth, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: That is, upon: there is no god but Allah.

* He said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: They embraced Islam, then did not associate anything with Him until they met Him.

* He said: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: They embraced Islam, then did not associate anything with Him until they met Him.

* Sa'd ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, regarding his words: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: They remained steadfast upon the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Others said: the meaning of that is: then they remained steadfast in His obedience.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, recited from the pulpit: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. He said: They remained steadfast, by Allah, in His obedience, and did not swerve the swerving of the fox.

* * *

His words: ﴿the angels will descend upon them﴾

He says: the angels will descend upon them at the time of the coming of death.

The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve"﴾. He said: at death.

* Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿the angels will descend upon them﴾. He said: at death.

* * *

His words: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve﴾

He says: the angels descend upon them, [saying] that you should not fear and not grieve; for the phrase is in the accusative position if that is its meaning.

It is reported from Abd Allah that he used to read it: "the angels descend upon them, saying: do not fear and do not grieve," meaning: they descend upon them saying, "Do not fear, and do not grieve." By His words ﴿Do not fear﴾ is meant what you are about to face after your death, and ﴿do not grieve﴾ over what you leave behind.

The people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, "Do not fear and do not grieve": He said: do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Hassan informed us, from Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve"﴾. He said: Do not fear what you are about to face of the matter of the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind of your worldly life, of family and children, for We will replace you in all of that.

It was said: this refers to the Hereafter.

Mention of those who said this:

* Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise"﴾. He said: that is in the Hereafter.

* * *

His words: ﴿but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised﴾

He says: rejoice that for you, in the Hereafter, is the Paradise which you were promised in the world for your faith in Allah and your steadfastness in His obedience.

As:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿but receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised﴾: in the world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 31–32:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿We are your protectors in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. In them you shall have what your souls desire, and in them you shall have what you ask for, as a welcome from the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, reporting the speech of His angels who descend upon these believers who remained upright in His obedience at the time of their death: ﴿We are your protectors﴾, O people, ﴿in the life of this world﴾, meaning: We used to support you therein. It has been mentioned that they are the guardian angels who used to record their deeds.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿We are your protectors in the life of this world﴾: "We are the guardian angels who were with you in the world, and we are your protectors in the Hereafter."

* *

As for His words: ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾

He says: And in the Hereafter also we are your protectors, just as we were your protectors in the world. He says: And in the Hereafter, with God, you shall have what your souls desire of delights and pleasures.

* *

As for His words: ﴿and in them you shall have what you ask for﴾

He says: And in the Hereafter you shall have what you ask for.

* *

As for His words: ﴿as a welcome from the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾

He says: Your Lord has given you that as a welcome for you, from a Lord who forgives your sins and is merciful to you by not punishing you after your repentance. The word *nuzulan* (welcome, hospitality) is in the accusative as a verbal noun (maṣdar) derived from the sense of His words: ﴿In them you shall have what your souls desire, and in them you shall have what you ask for﴾, because this implies: "Your Lord has bestowed upon you, with what you desire of bliss, a welcome."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 33–34:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteousness, and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ [41:33] ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil. Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ [41:34]

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: And who is better in speech, O people, than one who says, "Our Lord is Allah," then remains steadfast upon belief in Him, and adheres to His commands and prohibitions, and invites the servants of Allah to what he has said and acted upon of that.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the like of what we have said in this.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Hasan (al-Basri) recited, as transmitted by Ma'mar: "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteousness, and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'," and he said: "This is the beloved of Allah, this is the friend of Allah, this is the elect of Allah, this is the chosen one of Allah, this is the most beloved of creation to Allah. He answered Allah in His call, invited people to what Allah had answered in His call, acted righteously in his answering, and said, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims.' So this is the vicegerent of Allah."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah..." to the end of the verse, he said: "This is a servant whose deed confirms his speech, whose entrance is like his exit, whose secret is like his open, and whose witness is like his absence. Whereas the hypocrite is a servant whose deed contradicts his speech, whose entrance differs from his exit, whose secret differs from his open, and whose witness differs from his absence."

The people of knowledge differed concerning who is meant by this description among mankind. Some of them said: it refers to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah," he said: "Muhammad (ﷺ), when he invited to Islam."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah, does righteousness, and says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'," he said: "This is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."

And others said: it refers to the muadhdhin (the one who calls to prayer).

Mention of those who said that:

Dawud ibn Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Muktib al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Jarir al-Bajali narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, regarding the saying of God: "And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah," he said: "The muadhdhin." "And does righteousness," he said: "The prayer, what is between the adhan and the iqamah."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾

It means: and says, "Indeed, I am of those who submit to Allah in obedience, humble themselves to Him in servitude, and humble themselves before Him through belief in His oneness."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: The good deed of those who said "Our Lord is Allah" and then remained steadfast, who did well in their saying and in their answering, and who guided themselves to what He called them to of His obedience, and called the servants of Allah to the like of what they answered their Lord with, is not equal to the evil of those who said: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome﴾ [41:26]. Thus their states and stations are not equal in the sight of Allah; rather they differ, as He, exalted is His praise, described, that He distinguished between them. And He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾, repeating "lā" (not), and the meaning is: "the good is not equal, nor is the evil." Because whatever is not equal to something, then that thing to which it is unequal is not its equal, just as whatever is equal to something, then the other to which it is equal is equal to it; so one says: "So-and-so is equal to so-and-so," and "So-and-so has an equal." Likewise, "So-and-so is not equal to so-and-so," nor "so-and-so equal to him." Therefore I repeated "lā" with "the evil." Had it not been repeated with it, the sentence would still be sound. Some grammarians of Basra said: it is permissible to say that the second (lā) is superfluous; meaning: "The servant of Allah and Zayd are not equal," and the (second) lā is added for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power﴾ [57:29], meaning "so that they may know," and as He said: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and I swear by the reproaching soul﴾ [75:1–2]. Some of them rejected this view regarding ﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾ and regarding ﴿I swear﴾, saying: the second lā in ﴿that they have no power﴾ is returned to its place, because the negation attaches to "they are able" and not to "know," as one says: "I do not think Zayd will not stand," meaning, "I think Zayd will not stand." He said: Sometimes they make things certain by stating them at the beginning and the end, and sometimes they suffice with the first instead of the second.

It has been transmitted by hearing from the Arabs: "mā ka'annī a'rifuhā," meaning: "as if I do not know it." He said: As for the "lā" in His saying ﴿I swear﴾, it is a response, and the oath after it is a new beginning, and the particle of negation does not come as an introductory relative clause.

He only meant by His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾ that faith in Allah, acting in obedience to Him, is not equal to associating partners with Him and acting in disobedience to Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Repel, O Muhammad, with your forbearance the ignorance of the one who acts ignorantly toward you, and pardon the one who wrongs you with the wrong of the wrongdoer, and with your patience toward them, the hardship you find from them and what reaches you from their side.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said in this, though they differed in its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾, he said: "Allah commanded the believers to be patient at the time of anger, and to be forbearing and forgiving at the time of being wronged. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them as though he were a devoted friend."

And others said: the meaning of that is: repel with greeting toward the one who wrongs you with his wrong.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Amr, from Ata', regarding "Repel [evil] with that which is better," he said: "With greeting."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Mujahid, regarding "Repel [evil] with that which is better," he said: "Peace be upon you when you meet him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Do this which I have commanded you, O Muhammad, of repelling the evil of the one who wrongs you with your goodness which I have commanded you toward him; then the one who wronged you, between whom and you there is enmity, will become, from his gentleness toward you and his kindness to you, as though he were a devoted friend from among your paternal cousins, close in kinship to you. And "ḥamīm" means: close (qarīb).

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿as though he were a devoted friend﴾: that is, as though he were a close friend.
