As for His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: The good deed of those who said "Our Lord is Allah" and then remained steadfast, who did well in their saying and in their answering, and who guided themselves to what He called them to of His obedience, and called the servants of Allah to the like of what they answered their Lord with, is not equal to the evil of those who said: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it that you may overcome﴾ [41:26]. Thus their states and stations are not equal in the sight of Allah; rather they differ, as He, exalted is His praise, described, that He distinguished between them. And He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾, repeating "lā" (not), and the meaning is: "the good is not equal, nor is the evil." Because whatever is not equal to something, then that thing to which it is unequal is not its equal, just as whatever is equal to something, then the other to which it is equal is equal to it; so one says: "So-and-so is equal to so-and-so," and "So-and-so has an equal." Likewise, "So-and-so is not equal to so-and-so," nor "so-and-so equal to him." Therefore I repeated "lā" with "the evil." Had it not been repeated with it, the sentence would still be sound. Some grammarians of Basra said: it is permissible to say that the second (lā) is superfluous; meaning: "The servant of Allah and Zayd are not equal," and the (second) lā is added for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power﴾ [57:29], meaning "so that they may know," and as He said: ﴿I swear by the Day of Resurrection, and I swear by the reproaching soul﴾ [75:1–2]. Some of them rejected this view regarding ﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾ and regarding ﴿I swear﴾, saying: the second lā in ﴿that they have no power﴾ is returned to its place, because the negation attaches to "they are able" and not to "know," as one says: "I do not think Zayd will not stand," meaning, "I think Zayd will not stand." He said: Sometimes they make things certain by stating them at the beginning and the end, and sometimes they suffice with the first instead of the second.

It has been transmitted by hearing from the Arabs: "mā ka'annī a'rifuhā," meaning: "as if I do not know it." He said: As for the "lā" in His saying ﴿I swear﴾, it is a response, and the oath after it is a new beginning, and the particle of negation does not come as an introductory relative clause.

He only meant by His saying: ﴿And not equal are the good and the evil﴾ that faith in Allah, acting in obedience to Him, is not equal to associating partners with Him and acting in disobedience to Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Repel, O Muhammad, with your forbearance the ignorance of the one who acts ignorantly toward you, and pardon the one who wrongs you with the wrong of the wrongdoer, and with your patience toward them, the hardship you find from them and what reaches you from their side.

The people of interpretation said the like of what we have said in this, though they differed in its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better﴾, he said: "Allah commanded the believers to be patient at the time of anger, and to be forbearing and forgiving at the time of being wronged. When they do that, Allah protects them from Satan, and their enemy submits to them as though he were a devoted friend."

And others said: the meaning of that is: repel with greeting toward the one who wrongs you with his wrong.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Amr, from Ata', regarding "Repel [evil] with that which is better," he said: "With greeting."

Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Mujahid, regarding "Repel [evil] with that which is better," he said: "Peace be upon you when you meet him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then thereupon the one whom between you and him is enmity will become as though he were a devoted friend﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be exalted: Do this which I have commanded you, O Muhammad, of repelling the evil of the one who wrongs you with your goodness which I have commanded you toward him; then the one who wronged you, between whom and you there is enmity, will become, from his gentleness toward you and his kindness to you, as though he were a devoted friend from among your paternal cousins, close in kinship to you. And "ḥamīm" means: close (qarīb).

As:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿as though he were a devoted friend﴾: that is, as though he were a close friend.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 35–36:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ (35) ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾ (36)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And none is granted it" – it is not granted (yuʿṭā) to repel evil with good except those who are patient for the sake of Allah in the face of hardships and arduous matters. He said ﴿wa-mā yulaqqāhā﴾ (and none receives it) and did not say "wa-mā yulaqqāh" (and none receives it, masculine), because the meaning of the statement is: "none receives this act, i.e., repelling evil with what is better."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And none is granted it except one of great fortune⁠﴾.

He says: none receives this except one who has a share and a great fortune, for whom there is a prior advancement in good deeds.

As reported:

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿And none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾: "one of great fortune (dhū jadd)."

It has also been said that the great share which Allah, mighty is His praise, mentions in this verse for these people is Paradise.

Mention of those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Said related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient⁠﴾... the verse, and "the great share" is Paradise. It has been mentioned to us that a man insulted Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) while the Prophet (ﷺ) was present. He (Abu Bakr) pardoned him for a while, then anger overcame him and he retorted. The Prophet (ﷺ) then stood up and Abu Bakr followed him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, the man insulted me, and I pardoned and forgave while you were sitting; but when I began to retaliate, you stood up." The Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, an angel was repelling him from you, but when you came close to retaliating, the angel left and the Satan came, and by Allah, I would not sit with Satan, O Abu Bakr."

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muawiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune⁠﴾: he said: those for whom Allah has prepared Paradise.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah⁠﴾

... the verse. His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And if an evil suggestion from Satan should afflict you, O Muhammad, in your soul, a whispering from the discourse of the self, desiring to move you to requite the offender with an offence and calling you to harm him, then seek protection with Allah and take refuge from his steps. Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing of your seeking refuge from him and your seeking protection in Him from his whisperings, and of other than that from your speech and the speech of others; the All-Knowing of what Satan has cast into your soul of his whisperings, and what your soul has related to you of that, and what removes that from you, and other matters of yours and the affairs of His creation."

As reported:

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you⁠﴾, he said: "whispering and discourse of the self." ﴿So seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan⁠﴾.

* Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you⁠﴾: "this is anger."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 37:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And of His signs are the night and the day and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Among the proofs of Allah, exalted is He, over His creation, and His indication of His oneness and the greatness of His dominion, is the alternation of the night and the day, each of them succeeding the other, and the sun and the moon, neither the sun overtaking the moon, nor the night outpacing the day, and each in an orbit they swim. Do not prostrate, O people, to the sun or to the moon, for although they run in their orbit for your benefit, they run by means of what Allah makes them run for you, obeying Him in their running and their course, not by their own power to move and run without Allah's making them run and directing them, nor can they bring you benefit or harm. Rather, Allah has subjected them for your benefit and your welfare. So prostrate to Him, and worship Him alone, to the exclusion of them, for if He wills, He would obliterate their light, leaving you bewildered in darkness, not guided to a way and not seeing anything.

It has been said: ﴿who created them﴾ is in the plural with the pronoun "hunna" (them), because what is meant by the speech is: prostrate to Allah who created the night, the day, the sun and the moon, and that is plural. The pronoun for them is feminine, although it is the way of the Arabs, when they combine the masculine with the feminine, to render their pronoun in the masculine form, saying "akhawaka wa ukhtaka kallamani" (your two brothers and sisters spoke to me), and not "kallamnani." For it is their custom to make feminine the predicates of masculine non-human beings in the plural, saying: "I saw with 'Amr garments, so I took them (hunna) from him," and "The rings of Zayd pleased me; I took them (hunna) from him."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿if it is Him that you worship﴾

He says: If you worship Allah and submit to Him in obedience, and among obedience to Him is that you sincerely devote worship to Him, and do not associate with your obedience to Him and your worship of Him anything other than Him, for worship is not fitting for anything else and is not appropriate for anything besides Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 38:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire﴾ (38)

The Most High says: If they, O Muhammad, those among whom you live from the polytheists of Quraysh, are arrogant and magnify themselves against prostrating to God, who created them and created the sun and the moon, then the angels who are with your Lord are not arrogant about that, nor do they magnify themselves against it. Rather, they glorify Him and pray to Him night and day, ﴿and they never tire﴾, meaning: they do not cease from their worship, and they do not grow weary of prayer to Him.

The people of interpretation have said what we have said in this regard.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day﴾, he said: He means Muhammad; He says: "My servants," angels standing in rows, glorifying and not being arrogant.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 39:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who has revived it is the reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.﴾ (41:39)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And among the proofs of God and His evidences of His power to raise the dead after their decay, and to return them to their form as they were after their annihilation, is that you, O Muhammad, see the earth effaced and dust-colored, with no plant or crop in it.

As:

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren﴾: meaning dust-colored and crumbled.

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth barren﴾, he said: dry and crumbled.

﴿but when We send down water upon it, it stirs﴾: He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When We send down rain from the sky upon this barren earth, it stirs with plants. He says: it moves with them.

As:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿it stirs﴾, he said: with plants. ﴿and swells﴾, he says: it swells.

As:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and swells﴾, it swelled.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells﴾, it knows the rain by its softening and its swelling.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu Asim narrated to us, he said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿and swells﴾ for the plants, he said: it rose before it grew.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who has revived it is the reviver of the dead﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, He who revived this effaced earth, bringing forth plants from it and making it stir with crops after its dryness and effacement by the rain sent down upon it, is capable of reviving the dead of the children of Adam after their deaths by the water that descends from the sky for their revival.

The people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, he said: Just as He revives the earth with rain, so He revives the dead with water on the Day of Resurrection, between the two blasts. He means by this the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, He who has revived it is the reviver of the dead﴾.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is over all things competent﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, is, regarding the reviving of His creation after their deaths and regarding all that He wills, One of power whom nothing He wills can overpower, and for whom doing whatever He wishes is not impossible.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 40:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His mention: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do what you will; indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ (41:40)

His words, exalted is His mention, ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾ mean: indeed, those who incline away from the truth in Our proofs and evidences, and turn away from them, denying them and rejecting them.

I have already explained the meaning of ilhad (deviation, inclination away from the truth) in the past, with its supporting evidence, which makes repeating it here unnecessary.

We will mention some of the differences of opinion among those who differ concerning its meaning in this place.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the intended meaning of ilhad (deviation) in this place. Some of them said: it means the opposition of the polytheists to the Qur'an with noise and whistling, mocking it.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾, he said: al-muka' (whistling) and what is mentioned with it.

Others said: it means the report of their lying concerning the signs of God.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾, he said: they deny Our signs.

Others said: it means they are obstinate.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾, he said: they oppose: they are obstinate.

Others said: it means disbelief and polytheism.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs are not hidden from Us﴾, he said: these are the people of polytheism, and he said: ilhad is disbelief and polytheism.

Others said: it means the report of their altering the meanings of the Book of God.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words, ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs are not hidden from Us﴾, he said: it is placing speech in other than its place.

All these sayings we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of this are close in meaning, because ilhad and ilhad are inclination, and it may be inclination away from the signs of God and turning away from them by denying them; it may be by mocking them with whistling and clapping; it may be by separating from them and obstinacy; and it may be by distorting them and changing their meanings.

No saying is more correct regarding this than what we have said, and that the report about them should be general, that they deviated concerning the signs of God, as our Lord, blessed and exalted, generalized it.

* *

His words, ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: We know them, they are not hidden from Us, and We are watching them (lahum bil-mirsad) when they come to Us. This is a threat from God, exalted is His praise, to them, by His words: they will know when they come to Us what painful punishment of Ours they will meet. Then He, exalted is His praise, informed of what He will do with them when they come to Him, saying: ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ He, exalted is His mention, says to these who deviate concerning Our signs today in the world: the Day of Resurrection is the punishment of the Fire. Then God said: Is this one who is thrown into the Fire better, or the one who comes on the Day of Resurrection secure from the punishment of God because of his faith in God, exalted is His majesty? This disbeliever, if he believed in the signs of God and followed the command and prohibition of God, He would make him secure on the Day of Resurrection from what He warned him of, from His punishment, if he came to Him that day as a disbeliever.

* *

His words, ﴿Do what you will﴾

This too is a threat from God, issued in the form of a command. Likewise Mujahid used to say: Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Do what you will﴾, he said: this is a threat.

* *

His words, ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed God, O people, with your deeds that you do, is possessed of knowledge and awareness, nothing of them or of anything else is hidden from Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 41–42:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them—and indeed it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. It is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, those who denied this Qur'an and disbelieved in it when it came to them. By "the Reminder" He means the Qur'an.

As has been reported:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾: they disbelieved in the Qur'an.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And indeed this Reminder is a mighty Book, mighty by God's making it mighty, and by His preserving it from everyone who seeks to alter it, distort it, or change it, whether from humankind, jinn, or a rebellious devil.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾, he said: God made it mighty because it is His speech, and preserved it from falsehood.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾, he said: mighty against Satan.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: rejection cannot approach it from before it or from behind it.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, he said: rejection (nakir) from before it or from behind it.

Others said: the meaning of that is: Satan is unable to diminish from it any truth or add to it any falsehood. They said: "falsehood" is Satan.

* *

As for His words: ﴿from before it﴾

From the direction of truth. ﴿Or from behind it﴾: from the direction of falsehood.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾: "falsehood" is Iblis; he is unable to diminish from it any truth or add to it any falsehood.

Others said: its meaning is: falsehood is unable to add to it any letter or subtract from it any letter.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, he said: "falsehood" is Satan; he is unable to add a letter to it or subtract from it.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is that it should be said: its meaning is that no possessor of falsehood can, by his scheming, change it through his scheming or alter any part of its meanings from what it is, and that this is the approach from before it; nor can he attach to it what is not part of it, and that is its approach from behind it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾

He, the Exalted, says: It is a revelation from One possessing wisdom in managing His servants and directing them toward what serves their interests. ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ means: praised for His blessings upon them through His favors toward them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 41–42:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them—and indeed it is a mighty Book. Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it. It is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, those who denied this Qur'an and disbelieved in it when it came to them. By "the Reminder" He means the Qur'an.

As has been reported:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾: they disbelieved in the Qur'an.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾

He, the Exalted, says: And indeed this Reminder is a mighty Book, mighty by God's making it mighty, and by His preserving it from everyone who seeks to alter it, distort it, or change it, whether from humankind, jinn, or a rebellious devil.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾, he said: God made it mighty because it is His speech, and preserved it from falsehood.

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And indeed it is a mighty Book﴾, he said: mighty against Satan.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said: its meaning is: rejection cannot approach it from before it or from behind it.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, he said: rejection (nakir) from before it or from behind it.

Others said: the meaning of that is: Satan is unable to diminish from it any truth or add to it any falsehood. They said: "falsehood" is Satan.

* *

As for His words: ﴿from before it﴾

From the direction of truth. ﴿Or from behind it﴾: from the direction of falsehood.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾: "falsehood" is Iblis; he is unable to diminish from it any truth or add to it any falsehood.

Others said: its meaning is: falsehood is unable to add to it any letter or subtract from it any letter.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾, he said: "falsehood" is Satan; he is unable to add a letter to it or subtract from it.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is that it should be said: its meaning is that no possessor of falsehood can, by his scheming, change it through his scheming or alter any part of its meanings from what it is, and that this is the approach from before it; nor can he attach to it what is not part of it, and that is its approach from behind it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿It is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾

He, the Exalted, says: It is a revelation from One possessing wisdom in managing His servants and directing them toward what serves their interests. ﴿Praiseworthy﴾ means: praised for His blessings upon them through His favors toward them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 43:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you. Indeed, your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness and Possessor of painful punishment.﴾

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): What these polytheists, who deny you, say to you about what you have brought them from your Lord is nothing but what those nations before them said to their messengers before you. He says to him: So be patient with the harm you suffer from them, just as the resolute messengers (ulu al-'azm) were patient, ﴿and do not be like the companion of the fish﴾.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾: he consoles His Prophet (ﷺ), as you hear, saying: ﴿Likewise, no messenger came to those before them except that they said, "A magician or a madman."﴾

Muhammad narrated to us, he said: Ahmad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾, he said: They say nothing except what the polytheists said to the messengers before you.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness﴾

He says: Indeed your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness for the sins of those who repent to Him from their sins, by pardoning them, ﴿and Possessor of painful punishment﴾. He says: And He is Possessor of painful punishment for whoever persists in his disbelief and sins, dying while persisting in that before repenting of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 44:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Had We made it a Qur'an in a foreign tongue, they would have said: "Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?" Say: "It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing. As for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. Those are called from a distant place."﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: Had We made this Qur'an that We sent down, O Muhammad, a foreign tongue, your people from Quraysh would have said: ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail?﴾ meaning: why are its proofs and the verses it contains not made clear, so that we might understand it and know what it is and what is in it? ﴿What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?﴾ meaning that they would say, in denial of it: "Is this Qur'an foreign, while the tongue of the one to whom it was sent down is Arabic?"

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said concerning this verse, ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?﴾: "Had this Qur'an been foreign, they would have said: 'The Qur'an is foreign, and Muhammad is Arab.'"

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adiy narrated to me, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Ja'far ibn Abi Wahshiyyah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning this verse: ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?﴾ He said: "The messenger is Arab, and the tongue is foreign."

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: ﴿Had We made it a Qur'an in a foreign tongue, they would have said: Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?﴾ "A foreign Qur'an and an Arab tongue."

- Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mut'i', with similar wording.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail?﴾ He made it Arabic: the speech is foreign and the man is Arab.

- Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿Had We made it a Qur'an in a foreign tongue, they would have said: Why are its verses not explained in detail?﴾ He says: "Its verses were explained. 'What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?' We are an Arab people; what have we to do with foreignness?"

Others have differed from what we have mentioned from these, saying: the meaning of ﴿Why are its verses not explained in detail?﴾ is that some of it is Arabic and some of it is foreign. This interpretation accords with the reading of those who read ﴿a foreign tongue﴾ without the interrogative, taking it as a report from God about the statement of the polytheists, meaning: why are its verses not explained, some of them foreign, which the non-Arabs know, and some of them Arabic, which the Arabs understand.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: Quraysh said: "If only this Qur'an had been sent down foreign and Arabic." So God sent down: ﴿they would have said: Why are its verses not explained in detail? What, a foreign tongue and an Arab? Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾. And God sent down after this verse every tongue in which there is ﴿stones of baked clay﴾. He said: Persian, which was Arabized as sang and kal.

The readers of the metropolitan cities (qurra' al-amsar) read ﴿What, a foreign tongue and an Arab?﴾ in the interrogative form. It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he read it as "a'jamiyyun" with a single hamza, not in the interrogative sense, in the meaning we have mentioned from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is the reading upon which the readers of the metropolitan cities agree, since the consensus of the authorities (ijma' al-hujjah) rests upon it, in the interrogative form.

* *

His words: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: Say, O Muhammad, to them: "It," meaning by ﴿it﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿for those who believe﴾ in God and His Messenger, and who affirm what has come to them from their Lord, ﴿is guidance﴾, meaning a clarification of the truth, ﴿and healing﴾, meaning that it is healing from ignorance.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾: "God made it light, blessing and healing for the believers."

- Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, guidance and healing﴾: "The Qur'an."

* *

His words: ﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them﴾

Says He, may His remembrance be exalted: As for those who do not believe in God and His Messenger, and in what has come to them from God, there is heaviness in their ears from hearing this Qur'an, and deafness, so they do not listen to it, but turn away from it. ﴿And it is blindness for them﴾ means: this Qur'an is, upon the hearts of these deniers, blindness to it, so they do not see its proofs against them, nor what it contains of admonitions.

Ahl al-ta'wil said the same as what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them﴾: "They became blind and deaf to the Qur'an, so they do not benefit from it, nor desire it."

- Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears﴾: "Deafness." ﴿And it is blindness for them﴾: "Their hearts were blinded to it."

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And it is blindness for them﴾: "Blindness: disbelief."

The readers of the metropolitan cities read ﴿and it is blindness for them﴾ with a fatha on the mim. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he read "wa-huwa 'alayhim 'ami" with a kasra on the mim, as a description (na't) of the Qur'an.

The correct reading in this matter, in our view, is that upon which the readers of the metropolitan cities agree.

* *

His words: ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾

Ahl al-ta'wil differed about its meaning. Some of them said: the meaning of that is a comparison made by God, exalted is His praise, for the blindness of their hearts to understanding what was sent down in the Qur'an of its proofs and admonitions, to one who is far away: they are like one who is called from afar with a voice, but does not understand what was called out. Like the Arabs' saying to a man of little understanding: "You are being called from afar," and their saying to one who grasps things quickly: "You take matters from near."

Those who said so:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from one of his companions, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾: "Distant from their hearts."

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, with similar wording.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾: "They wasted the chance to accept the matter when it was near, by repenting and believing, whereupon it would have been accepted from them, but they refused."

Others said: rather, the meaning of that is that on the Day of Resurrection they will be called from a place distant from them by their most abominable names.

Those who said so:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'jlah, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, concerning ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾: "A man is called by his most abominable name."

The grammarians of Arabic differed about the point at which His words ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾ are complete. Some of them said: its completion is ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾, and the advocates of this view made the predicate of ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾ to be ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: this is permissible, and it is also permissible that it be upon the reports in the Qur'an that stand without a predicate, as some things stand without a predicate when the speech is long and the meaning is known, such as His words: ﴿And if a Qur'an had been such that the mountains were set moving by it, or the earth were split asunder by it...﴾ and what is similar to that.

He said: a shaykh of the people of knowledge narrated to me, saying: I heard 'Isa ibn 'Umar ask 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd about ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾: where is its predicate? 'Amr said: its meaning in interpretation is: indeed those who disbelieved in the Reminder when it came to them disbelieved in it, ﴿and indeed it is a Book of might﴾. 'Isa said: "You have done well, O Abu 'Uthman."

Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: if you wish, you may make the response to ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾ to be ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾; and if you wish, its response is in His words ﴿and indeed it is a Book of might﴾, so that its response is known, and it is omitted. The first of the two options is the more grammatical and more similar to what has come in the Qur'an.

Others said: rather, this is among what has turned away from the report about what was begun to the report about the Reminder that follows it. On this view, the report about those who disbelieve in the Reminder is left out, and the report about the Reminder is made the completion, namely: ﴿and indeed it is a Book of might﴾. So the meaning of the speech for the proponent of this view is: that the Reminder which these polytheists disbelieved in, when it came to them, and indeed it is a Book of might. He compared it to His words: ﴿And those of you who die and leave wives behind, they shall wait by themselves...﴾.

The view that I find closest to the truth on this matter is that it is said: it is among what has been left without its report, being content with the hearers' knowledge of its meaning once the speech had grown long.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 45:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it. And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them. And indeed they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt.﴾

His saying, exalted is He and remembered is His mention: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾ — O Muhammad — meaning the Torah, just as We gave you the Furqan (the criterion, i.e., the Qur'an). ﴿But differences arose concerning it﴾ — meaning: differences arose regarding acting upon what is in it among those of the Jews who were given it. ﴿And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them﴾ — meaning: had it not been for what had preceded of God's decree and judgment concerning them, that He would delay their punishment until the Day of Resurrection.

As:

* Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: ﴿And had it not been for a word that had preceded from your Lord﴾, he said: They were delayed until the Day of Resurrection.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And indeed they are, concerning it, in disquieting doubt﴾

Meaning: and indeed the deviating faction among them is in doubt about what they said concerning it, ﴿disquieting﴾ — meaning: their saying about it, what they said, troubles them, because they said it without certainty, and they only said it as conjecture.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 46:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against it. And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Whoever acts in obedience to God in this world, complying with His command and refraining from what He has forbidden, ﴿it is for his own soul﴾, meaning: the benefit of that righteous deed is for his own soul, because he will be repaid for it, and so he deserves in the Hereafter from God Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, meaning: whoever commits acts of disobedience to God in it, it is upon his own soul that he inflicts harm, because by that he earns for it the wrath of God and painful punishment. ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾. He, the Exalted, says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, does not impose the punishment for one sinner's sin upon someone other than the one who earned it; rather, He punishes no one except for the crime that he committed in this world, or for a cause that he deserved from Him. And God knows best.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 47:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. And no fruit emerges from its coverings, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. And the Day He will call to them, "Where are My partners?" they will say, "We have informed You that none of us is a witness."﴾ (41:47)

Exalted is His remembrance, says: To Allah is referred the knowledge of the Hour by those who know it, for none knows when it will occur except Him. ﴿And no fruit emerges from its coverings﴾ means: nor does any fruit appear from a tree's sheaths (akmam) in which it was hidden, emerging out from them into view. ("And what a female bears") means: nor does any female bear a pregnancy when she carries it, nor give birth to her offspring, except with knowledge from Allah, nothing of that being hidden from Him.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of His words: ﴿And no fruit emerges from its coverings﴾.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, ﴿from their coverings﴾, he said: "When they appear."

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And no fruit emerges from its coverings﴾, he said: "From its spathe (tal'ihā). The akmam is the plural of kumma (sheath), which is every container for water or other things; and the Arabs call the husk of the cotton-bud (kafra) a kumm." [[Probably the original reads: plural of kumm, without a ta' marbuta, since akmam is the plural of "kumm" and not of "kumma". See Lisan al-Arab: k-m-m.]]

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of His words ﴿min thamarat﴾. The readers of Medina recited it ﴿min thamarat﴾ in the plural, while the readers of Kufa recited "min thamara" in the singular. Whichever of the two recitations is read, it is correct in our view, since their meanings are close, and both are well known in recitation.

And His words: ﴿And the Day He will call to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾

Exalted is His remembrance, says: And the Day Allah calls those who associated others with Him in the world, the idols and images: "Where are My partners whom you associated with Me in your worship of Me?" ﴿They will say, "We have informed You"﴾ means: we have made You aware, ﴿that none of us is a witness﴾ means: those polytheists said to their Lord on that day: none of us is a witness testifying that You have a partner.

The people of interpretation have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿adhannaka﴾, he said: "It means: we informed You."

Muhammad narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: ﴿We have informed You, none of us is a witness﴾, they said: "We have made You hear (atana-ka)" [[As it stands in the original. Probably "atlana-ka" (we have made You know), so that it carries the meaning of knowledge.]] that none of us is a witness that You have a partner.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 48–49:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those they used to call upon before will vanish from them, and they will be certain that there is for them no place of escape﴾ (41:48) ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good, but if evil touches him, then he is despairing and hopeless﴾ (41:49).

His saying, may He be remembered: "And those they used to call upon before will vanish from them" means: the gods that these polytheists used to worship in the world will be lost to them on the Day of Resurrection. They take a path other than their path, so they do not benefit them and do not avert from them any of the punishment of God that has descended upon them.

* *

His saying: ﴿and they will be certain that there is for them no place of escape﴾

He means: they will then be certain that they have no refuge, that is, there is no place for them to take refuge from the punishment of God.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and they will be certain that there is for them no place of escape﴾: they will be certain that there is no refuge for them.

Scholars of Arabic grammar differed about the reason why the verb of thinking (ẓann) was nullified in this place. Some of the people of Basra said that it was nullified because the meaning of His saying ﴿and they thought﴾ is "they were certain." He said: "ma" here is a particle, not a noun, and a verb does not govern something of this kind; therefore the verb was made inoperative. Others said: a verb does not become inoperative while it still governs in meaning except for a reason. He said: the reason is that it is a report; so when it falls upon something it does not govern, it becomes a report and a supposition, and when it governs, it remains in its original state.

* *

His saying: ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: the disbeliever in God does not tire of supplicating for good, that is, of asking good of his Lord. The good in this place is wealth and bodily health; he means: he does not tire of seeking that. ﴿But if evil touches him﴾ means: if harm reaches him in his person, through illness or hardship in his livelihood, or the withholding of his provision, ﴿then he is despairing and hopeless﴾ means: he is in despair of the mercy and relief of God, hopeless of His mercy, and of that harm that has descended upon him being lifted from him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good﴾: he says, the disbeliever. ﴿But if evil touches him, then he is despairing and hopeless﴾: hopeless of good.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Man does not tire﴾: he does not grow weary. It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: "Man does not tire of supplicating for good" (لا يَسْأَمُ الإنْسَانُ مِنْ دَعَاءٍ بالخَيْرِ).

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those they used to call upon before will vanish from them, and they will be certain that there is for them no place of escape﴾ (41:48) ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good, but if evil touches him, then he is despairing and hopeless﴾ (41:49).

He said: "ma" here is a particle, not a noun, and a verb does not govern something of this kind; therefore the verb was made inoperative. Others said: a verb does not become inoperative while it still governs in meaning except for a reason. He said: the reason is that it is a report; so when it falls upon something it does not govern, it becomes a report and a supposition, and when it governs, it remains in its original state.

* *

His saying: ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good﴾

He, may He be remembered, means: the disbeliever in God does not tire of supplicating for good, that is, of asking good of his Lord. The good in this place is wealth and bodily health; he means: he does not tire of seeking that. ﴿But if evil touches him﴾ means: if harm reaches him in his person, through illness or hardship in his livelihood, or the withholding of his provision, ﴿then he is despairing and hopeless﴾ means: he is in despair of the mercy and relief of God, hopeless of His mercy, and of that harm that has descended upon him being lifted from him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Man does not tire of supplicating for good﴾: he says, the disbeliever. ﴿But if evil touches him, then he is despairing and hopeless﴾: hopeless of good.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Man does not tire﴾: he does not grow weary. It is mentioned that in the reading of Abdullah it is: "Man does not tire of supplicating for good" (لا يَسْأَمُ الإنْسَانُ مِنْ دَعَاءٍ بالخَيْرِ).

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after some adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is my due. And I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." But We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe torment.﴾ (41:50)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: If We were to remove from this disbeliever the affliction that had befallen him of sickness in his body and hardship, and distress and toil in his livelihood, out of mercy from Us, granting him health in his body after sickness, and providing him with wealth, expanding his livelihood after toil and hardship: ﴿he will surely say, "This is my due"﴾ with Allah, because Allah is pleased with me on account of my deeds, and I am deserving of it, and I am established upon it.

As related:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿he will surely say, "This is my due"﴾: that is, because of my deeds, and I am entitled to this. He says: "And I do not think the Hour will ever come" — that is, "Nor do I suppose the Resurrection will come on the day it arrives." He says: "And even if it does come, and I am returned to Allah alive after my death." He says: "Indeed I have with Him wealth and property."

As related:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words: ﴿Indeed I have with Him the best﴾: he says: "wealth." He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: We will surely inform these disbelievers in Allah, who wish vain things from Him, on the day they return to Him, of what they did in the world of acts of disobedience and the evil deeds they committed; then We will surely recompense all of them for that, with their recompense.

And that severe torment is their remaining eternally in the Fire of Hell, where they will neither die nor live.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 51:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication.﴾

Exalted is He, mentioning Himself, says: And when We bestow favor upon the disbeliever, relieving him of the harm that was upon him, granting him wealth and abundance, and giving him bodily health and well-being, he turns away from what We have called him to of obedience, and withdraws from it, ﴿and distances himself﴾, meaning: he keeps far from answering Us to what We have called him to. By "his side" (janb) is meant his direction (nahiyah).

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: ﴿he turns away and distances himself﴾, he said: "Turns away" means he turns his face away, and "distances himself" means he moves far away.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication﴾

By "lengthy" ('arid) is meant: abundant.

As:

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿he is one of lengthy supplication﴾, he said: "abundant." This is like the people's saying: "So-and-so lengthened the supplication," when he increased it; and likewise, "he made his supplication broad (a'rada du'a'ahu)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verses 52–53:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you have disbelieved in it, who is further astray than one who is in extreme opposition?﴾ (52)

Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾ (O Muhammad) to those who deny what I have brought them from your Lord of this Qur'an, ﴿Have you considered﴾ (O people), ﴿if it is from Allah, and you have disbelieved in it﴾ (that which you deny), ﴿are you not in division and far from the right?﴾ He put the informing in place of the separation, saying: ﴿who is further astray than one who is in extreme opposition?﴾ when its meaning is understood.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿who is further astray than one who is in extreme opposition?﴾

He says: Say to them, who is more greatly departed from the intended path and more inclined to other than the way of truth, than one who is in division from the command of Allah and in opposition to Him, far from right guidance?

* *

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ (53)

Allah, the Exalted, says: We shall show these deniers what We sent down to Muhammad, Our servant, of the Reminder, Our signs on the horizons.

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of the signs which Allah promised these people that He would show them. Some of them said: By the signs on the horizons is meant the victories of the Prophet (ﷺ) in the regions of the land of the polytheists, from the people of Makkah and its outskirts, and by His saying: ﴿and within themselves﴾ is meant the conquest of Makkah.

Those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from al-Minhal, concerning His saying: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons﴾ he said: the dominance of Muhammad (ﷺ) over the people.

Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons﴾, he says: what We will open for you, O Muhammad, of the horizons, ﴿and within themselves﴾ (meaning) among the people of Makkah, he says: We will open Makkah for you.

Others said: By that is meant that He would show them the stars of the night and its moon, and the sun of the day, and that is what He promised them He would show them on the horizons. They said: By the horizons is meant the horizons of the heaven, and by His saying: ﴿and within themselves﴾ is meant the passage of excrement and urine.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾ he said: the horizons of the heavens: their stars, their sun and their moon which run, and signs within themselves also.

The most correct of these two views is the first, which is what al-Suddi said, because Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, promised His Prophet (ﷺ) that He would show these polytheists who were deniers of him signs on the horizons. It is not sensible that the threat would be that He would show them what they already see; rather, it must be a promise from Him to them that He would show them what they had not seen before: the dominance of the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) over the outskirts of their land and over their land itself. As for the stars, the sun and the moon, they had seen them often before and after, and there is no sense in threatening them with showing them that.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾

He, may His praise be exalted, says: We shall show these polytheists Our victories in their regions and among them, until they know the reality of what We sent down to Muhammad and revealed to him of the promise to him that We shall make prevail what We have sent him with of religion over all religions, even though the polytheists dislike it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord, O Muhammad, that He is a witness over everything that His creatures do, nothing of which escapes His knowledge, and He will recompense them for their deeds, rewarding the good-doer with good and the evil-doer with its due?

Concerning His saying: ﴿annahu﴾ there are two possibilities:

The first: that it is in the genitive position by way of repeating the particle "bi" (with), so the meaning of the sentence becomes: Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is a witness over every thing? The second: that it is in the nominative position, governed by "yakfi" (suffices), so the meaning of the sentence becomes: Is it not sufficient for your Lord that His witnessing is over every thing?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 41, verse 54:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is all-encompassing of everything.﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Unquestionably, these deniers of the signs of God are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord, meaning that they are in doubt about the resurrection after death and their return to their Lord.

As related:

* Muhammad related to us, saying: Ahmad related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Indeed, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾: he said, "In doubt."

* *

And His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, He is all-encompassing of everything﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Unquestionably, indeed God is all-encompassing of everything He has created, in knowledge of all of it and in power over it. No knowledge of anything He wills escapes Him so that it eludes Him; rather, the one who has power over it is the one who knows its place.

End of the commentary on Surah Fussilat.
